title: S1-017 responsibility vocabulary and claim boundaries (authoritative, versioned)

vocabulary.actor: observed principal/process; always a canonical principal ID, never a display name
vocabulary.authority: capability/approval/lease verified by the gateway; the only allow/deny source
vocabulary.choice_point: a model state where the bounded model enumerates admissible alternatives
vocabulary.available_alternative: an action provably available in the bounded transition model
vocabulary.attempt: a request that could have been granted or denied
vocabulary.causal_contribution: a link inside the declared causal model, never inferred from ordering alone
vocabulary.stit_attribution: the agent sees to it that a formula holds in the declared model (choice made a difference)
vocabulary.atl_ability: a coalition holds a strategy forcing a temporal objective in the declared game (environment quantified adversarially)
vocabulary.operational_accountability: audit binds actor, authority, request, decision and effect/absence marker
vocabulary.responsibility_annotation: derived explanation with provenance and confidence; authority=false always
vocabulary.legal_moral_blame: OUT_OF_SCOPE, always; no model output may assert it

confidence_rule: PROVEN requires exhaustive evaluation over the declared bounded state space; anything less is SUPPORTED at most; incomplete traces, ambiguous alternatives or model disagreement force UNDERDETERMINED (abstain, never guess)
underdetermination_rule: when available alternatives cannot be rebuilt from audit data, the answer is UNDERDETERMINED. Absence of an event never proves absence of a possibility. Correlation/ordering never proves causation without a model rule.

hard_invariants.R1: gateway ownership: 100% of runtime authorization decisions belong to Gateway/Gate; analytics is absent from the allow/deny path
hard_invariants.R2: non-authority: an annotation creates no capability, grant, approval, lease, policy, scope, task transition or terminal decision
hard_invariants.R3: immutable evidence: analytics never mutates source audit/lineage rows; a correction is a new annotation + supersedes
hard_invariants.R4: trace binding: every conclusion binds an exact immutable trace digest, actor, goal, scope, model and corpus version
hard_invariants.R5: complete authority chain: attribution needs actor, request, exact action/args, decision, grant/denial/revocation and effect/absence marker
hard_invariants.R6: alternatives provenance: each alternative is proven by the transition model or marked UNKNOWN; producer summary never suffices
hard_invariants.R7: revocation awareness: post-revoke action is never explained by the old grant without an explicit violation; revoked authority is not available
hard_invariants.R8: delegation completeness: child attribution carries delegator, delegation chain, scope, expiry/revocation and exact allowed actions
hard_invariants.R9: no identity collapse: actor, worker, delegator, approver and service principal never merge over display names
hard_invariants.R10: underdetermination: incomplete traces, ambiguous alternatives or model disagreement abstain instead of attributing confidently
hard_invariants.R11: privacy/scope: analysis/export reveals no hidden scopes, principals, content or alternatives; redaction is visible and counted
hard_invariants.R12: reproducibility: identical frozen inputs give identical semantic results; provenance mismatch blocks comparison/publication
hard_invariants.R13: no overclaim: formal results speak only for the declared bounded model/state space, never as facts about arbitrary worlds
hard_invariants.R14: audit reconstruction: the decision rebuilds from raw canonical events without trusting producer verdict/summary

forbidden: STIT/ATL result, score or explanation changing ALLOW/DENY
absence of alternatives read as fault or responsibility
post-hoc annotation rewriting a source event or history
probabilistic/heuristic inference published as proven fact
the model named as a legal, moral or production-conformance oracle
